system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: task = lr.Task(agent, name="Bot", system_message="You are a helpful assistant")
system_prompt_style.note: System message supplied per-Task; tool instructions appended for native ToolMessage.

env_context_strategy.evidence_locator: README.md (Define an agent, set up a task, and run it)
env_context_strategy.note: General framework; DocChatAgent adds embedding_rag via vecdb, reachable by config.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Langroid tries to shorten the message history by dropping early messages
context_compaction.evidence_locator: docs/FAQ.md (How langroid handles long chat histories)
context_compaction.note: Tool result truncation via optional parameters in ToolMessage (large-tool-results).

observation_format.evidence_quote:
Multimodal support, i.e. allow PDF, image
inputs to LLM.
observation_format.note: Default observations are text; image input reachable.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote:
use_tools=False, # don't use Langroid native tool
use_functions_api=True, # use OpenAI function-call API

tool_count.evidence_locator: README.md (Define an agent, set up a task, and run it)
tool_count.note: Default ChatAgent has no tools enabled; tools added via enable_message.

edit_primitive.note: No built-in file-edit tool shipped by default; an EditTool is mentioned only in plugin prose.

tool_schema_source.note: MCP adapter converts server tools into ToolMessage instances.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote:
MCP Support: Allow any LLM-Agent to leverage MCP Servers via Langroid's simple
[MCP tool adapter]

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
manages iteration over an Agent's responder methods,
and orchestrates multi-agent interactions
loop_primitives.note: batch task runs give multi_attempt-like parallelism.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: gives the agent instructions (or roles, or goals)
planning_granularity.note: No default plan object; planner workflows are examples.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_locator: README.md (Define an agent, set up a task, and run it)
multi_agent_topology.note: hierarchical sub-task delegation reachable via add_sub_task.

delegation_mechanism.note: Default single task has no delegation; subagent_spawn reachable via TaskTool/add_sub_task.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote:
the `task` has been set up with `interactive=True`
(which is the default). With this setting, the task loop waits for user input

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The [Agent](https://langroid.github.io/langroid/reference/agent/base/#langroid.agent.base.Agent) class encapsulates LLM conversation state

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Currently there is no built-in Langroid mechanism for this
long_term_memory.evidence_locator: docs/FAQ.md (Can I persist agent state across multiple runs?)
long_term_memory.note: vector-store is for RAG documents, not cross-run agent memory.

state_persistence.evidence_quote:
Currently there is no built-in Langroid mechanism for this, but you can
achieve a basic type of persistence by saving the agent's `message_history`
state_persistence.note: Portable JSON chat-history snapshots added in 0.66.0.

self_verification.evidence_quote: LanceRAGTaskCreator creates 3-agent RAG system with Query Planner, Critic and RAG Agent
self_verification.note: Critic agents are optional patterns; no harness-enforced verification by default.

retry_policy.evidence_quote:
this method
ensures that tool generation errors are sent back to the LLM so it retries the generation
retry_policy.note: Only step-level tool-format retries, not task-level retries.

rollback.evidence_quote:
a new tool, `RewindTool`,
that lets an agent "rewind and redo" a past message
rollback.note: RewindTool rewinds conversation, not filesystem/repo changes.

termination_condition.evidence_quote:
have `max_cost`
and `max_tokens` params to exit when tokens or cost exceed a limit
termination_condition.note: Infinite loop detection for cycles <=10; done_sequences and turns cap steps; max_time budgets.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Langroid supports [Redis](https://redis.com/try-free/) to cache LLM responses.
cost_controls.note: Portkey/LangDB gateways provide routing; max_cost/max_tokens the budget.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: and code is executed using Langroid's tool/function-call mechanism
execution_isolation.note: Tool handlers run in-process in the host Python; a Docker image of examples is offered.

filesystem_access.note: No filesystem sandboxing in-process; boundary is the host process.

network_policy.evidence_quote: [`GoogleSearchTool`](https://github.com/langroid/langroid/blob/main/langroid/agent/tools/google_search_tool.py) to enable Agents (their LLM) to do Google searches

permission_model.evidence_quote:
the task loop waits for user input after
either the `llm_response` or `agent_response` (typically a tool-handling response)
permission_model.note: Default interactive=True gates each step; interactive=False -> none.

tracing.evidence_quote:
Langroid generates detailed logs of multi-agent interactions and
maintains provenance/lineage of messages
tracing.note: HTML Logger (0.57.0); Portkey gives external observability.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote:
`Langroid` is an intuitive, lightweight, extensible and principled
Python framework to easily build LLM-powered applications
eval_hooks.note: No benchmark evaluation runner in the repo tree listing.

guardrails.evidence_quote: generalized taint propagation across tool re-emission paths

target_domain.note: web crawling/search tools; MCP generic tools; RAG document QA.

first_release_date.note: Earliest releases listed are July 2023 (0.1.24-0.1.30); exact first tag date not in evidence.
